title: Стихи против гнева и совет для Луи  (Poetry Against Anger and Advice for Louis)

segments.t: Tamara Ivanovna instructs Viktor Petrovich to recite a poem out loud every time he feels a wave of anger rising. Back at Claude Monet, a desperate Louis asks Max how to get rid of his persistent female admirer, and Max suggests telling her the simple truth.
При каждом приступе ярости вы читаете стихотворение.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
При каждом приступе ярости вы читаете стихотворение.
'With every fit of rage, you recite a poem.' Focusing on a poem at once, Louis centers the remark on "stikhotvoreniye" ("a poem") without any extra fuss.
'Just give it a try.' Pushing back earnestly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Well, for example, any poem at all.' Louis responds frankly in this moment, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'Well, that one.' Weighing in plainly in front of Louis, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I know that one.' Weighing in quietly before Max, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Now it cries like a little child.' Max opens up lightly around Louis, watching Louis's face to see how the news lands.
'Well, there you see.' Louis cuts in smoothly in front of Max and chooses "vidite" ("see", from the root "videt") so Max hears the exact meaning.
'I really want to, very much.' Reacting directly around Louis, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'You mean me.' Louis answers evenly toward Max, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'How do I get rid of her?' Max jumps in boldly at once and puts the emphasis on "izbavitsya" ("to get rid of") in the middle of the talk.
'Just tell her that you are, well, that way.' Louis responds frankly during the talk, watching Max's face to see how the news lands.
'You know, not into girls.' Max reacts steadily with Louis, before Louis can change the subject.
'Come sit down with us.' Louis weighs in decisively around Max and chooses "sadis" ("sit down", from the root "saditsya") so Max hears the exact meaning.
При каждом приступе ярости вы читаете стихотворение.

That wraps up this scene as tamara teaches Chef Barinov to recite poetry whenever rage strikes, while in the kitchen Max advises Louis on how to gently turn down his persistent female admirer. See you next time!
